name: North Dakota
nameStory: Dakota is the Sioux word for 'friend' or 'ally' - what the Dakota people called themselves. Two states are named Friend, north and south.
capitalStory: The town was called Edwinton until 1873, when the railroad renamed it Bismarck to flatter the German chancellor Otto von Bismarck and attract German money. It worked. A US state capital is named after a foreign politician as a marketing move.
funFacts: Nobody knows whether North or South Dakota is really the 39th state. President Harrison shuffled the two papers before signing so no one could tell, and they are listed alphabetically.
The Red River flows north, which is why it floods so badly: the southern end thaws first and the meltwater runs straight into ice still blocking the north.
Rugby, North Dakota claims to be the geographic center of North America.
Theodore Roosevelt credited his time ranching in the North Dakota Badlands with making him president.
